The [[Coppa Italia]] is an annual [[association football|football]] cup competition established in Italy in [[1922 Coppa Italia|1922]]. The competition is open to all [[Serie A]] and [[Serie B]] clubs, as well as four teams from [[Serie C]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 June 2021 |title=Coppa Italia, ecco il nuovo format: il regolamento ufficiale |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/coppa-italia/coppa-italia-regolamento-2021-2024 |access-date=9 June 2021 |website=[[Sky Sport (Italy)|Sky Sport]] |language=it |archive-date=18 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218172858/https://sport.sky.it/calcio/coppa-italia/coppa-italia-regolamento-2021-2024 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Since the first final between [[FC Vado|Vado]] and [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] in [[1922 Coppa Italia final|1922]], 78 finals have taken place. There have been 44 single-match finals, one of which was replayed after the initial game ended in a goalless draw.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last1=Kramarsic |first1=Igor |last2=Di Maggio |first2=Roberto |date=27 May 2021 |title=Italy – List of Cup Finals |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/italcuphist.html |access-date=25 May 2023 |publisher=RSSSF|archive-date=3 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230203102729/https://rsssf.org/tablesi/italcuphist.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 30 occasions, the final two teams played against each other over two legs on a home-and-away basis.<ref name=":0" /> On four occasions, a final group of four teams played a double round-robin tournament to determine the winners.<ref name=":0" /> As of 2026, 26 different teams have competed in the final, with 16 of them winning the competition at least once. On 12 occasions, the winning team also won Serie A in the same season, thus making a domestic [[Double (association football)|double]]. [[Inter Milan]] are the only team to win Serie A, Coppa Italia and [[UEFA Champions League]] in the same year, in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Inter join exclusive treble club |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c50f4b42c3a-0fbc1831ccbe-1000--inter-join-exclusive-treble-club/ |publisher=[[UEFA]] |access-date=16 August 2022 |date=22 May 2010 |archive-date=18 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218173040/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c50f4b42c3a-0fbc1831ccbe-1000--inter-join-exclusive-treble-club/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The tournament was not held in the years 1923–1925, 1928–1935 and 1944–1957.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Calzaretta |first=Nicola |title=I colori della vittoria |publisher=Goalbook Edizioni |year=2014 |isbn=978-88-908115-9-3 |location=[[Pisa]] |language=it}}</ref> It was recommenced in 1958, in conjunction with the UEFA project for a new competition, the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]].<ref name=":1" />

The [[Stadio Olimpico]] of [[Rome]] has hosted the most finals (44); since 2008, all finals have been held there in the form of a single-leg match, with the exception of the [[2021 Coppa Italia final|2021 final]], which was held at the [[Mapei Stadium – Città del Tricolore]] in [[Reggio Emilia]].<ref name=":0" /> The cities to host the final the fewest times are [[Vado Ligure]], [[Venice]], [[Ancona]], [[Vicenza]] and Reggio Emilia (once each).<ref name=":0" /> [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] hold the record for the most wins with 15, the highest number of consecutive victories in the final (4), and most appearances in the final (22). [[AC Milan]] have lost the most finals (10).<ref name=":0" /> Of the teams who have participated in more than one final, [[Palermo FC|Palermo]] and [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]] share the worst win–loss record with three defeats and no victories each. Of the victorious teams, [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] have the lowest percentage of success, winning one out of six finals (16.67 per cent).<ref name=":0" /> Two teams from outside the top league have won the cup: Vado in 1922 (from [[Promozione]]{{Efn|At that time, this championship was the second tier of the [[Italian football league system]].}}) and [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] in 1962 (from Serie B).

The highest-scoring final was the first leg between [[AS Roma|Roma]] and Inter Milan in [[2007 Coppa Italia final|2007]], with eight goals.<ref name=":0" /> On seven occasions, the result was a goalless draw, four of which were a single-leg final.<ref name=":0" /> The match with the largest margin of victory was the second leg between [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] and [[US Ancona 1905|Ancona]] in 1994, which Sampdoria won 6–1.<ref name=":0" /> Seven finals have been decided by a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], the most recent being between Napoli and Juventus in [[2020 Coppa Italia final|2020]].<ref name=":0" /> The current winners are Inter Milan, who beat [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] 2–0 in the [[2026 Coppa Italia final|2026 final]].<ref name=":0" />
